correctness.rationale: Explicit positive Fourier multipliers make I−σ_N injective modulo constants; Jordan product coupling and strict Hilbert convexity reduce all real BV extrema to arcs. Parseval yields an exact N-dependent Fourier sum. Local-uniform Riemann convergence gives the sinc/sine-integral profile. Derivative signs isolate one root below 2π, while a rational arctan+Si certificate shows Φ(π) above the rigorous 1/q² upper bound for all q≥2π. Summation by parts excludes unbounded scaled maximizing gaps, forcing all optimizers to the unique q*. The standalone checker confirmed the rational certificate and 40 finite tests; no finite experiment was substituted for the analytic limit.

value.rationale: A natural positive Fourier smoothing operator has a new sharp BV→L2 asymptotic norm, including exact universal constant, complete finite-N reduction, rigidity of every norming input, and concentration of two discontinuities at a non-obvious 1/N separation. This is quantitatively stronger than a convergence rate and structurally contrasts with semicircle maximizers for the L1 error. It is directly motivated by spectral smoothing of discontinuous signals; no artificial parameter slice or arbitrary finite computation.
